subject: not all apps updatable on Spark server

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: not all apps updatable on Spark server
parts:
Hi,

In the past few days I was running some git pull commands on Spark to update content for three apps. I was simply adding the same generic text statement to each app. Although all three files were updated on Spark, only two of the three apps show the updated text in the browser when visiting the app url. For the third app, no changes I make have any effect, even though I ssh onto Spark and cat the file contents to my screen and confirm they have in fact been updated in the server.

Recently, I had the same trouble with just one app (a different one this time) on our local instance of shiny-server that I use for app development and testing. In that case, we could not figure out the problem, but when our IT person rebooted shiny-server, he problem was fixed. Is there some kind of caching going on? I do believe we still run the older version of shiny-server locally, so it may not be an issue in the newer version. However, I am having the inability to run updated files for one app now on Spark.

The app with the problem: http://spark.rstudio.com/uafsnap/temp_wind_events/

The last git pull was three days ago. The text on the 'About' tab in the app does not show the updated text in the app's about.r file on Spark.

Matt

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: not all apps updatable on Spark server
parts:
Hi Matt,

It depends on how you are creating the objects for your shiny application. Please refer to: 

http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping

for some information on the scope of objects. You could have defined objects that are shared and therefore not updated for each browser access. Do you see any difference in your 3 apps in terms of scope of objects?

Let us know with more detail (possibly sample code) if you continue having problem with your app.

Fereshteh

parts:
Hi Fereshteh

There is a similarity regarding the way I load this particular content, and a difference to how I load other (seemingly) unrelated app data. The way in which I load the content for the 'About' tab is the same in all apps, for example, in ui.R (excess code removed)

tabPanelAbout <- source("about.r")$value
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel(
                ...
        ),
        sidebarPanel(
               ...
        ),
        mainPanel(
                tabsetPanel(
                        tabPanel("Conditional Barplots",plotOutput("plot",height="auto"),value="barplots"),
                        tabPanelAbout(),
                        id="tsp"
                )
        )

This is the same in all my apps, and has been in place many months. The only difference regarding scoping that I can think of is that in the server.R script for this app, I force some global assignments of datasets loaded by a user, inside the shinyServer call. But this seems completely unrelated. In any case, it has been in place a long time but I have never had this issue before. And the app this happened with on our local instance of shiny-server had no such global scoping.

If it is possible that this can prevent other things from being updated, here is the code inside the shinyServer call that is unique to this app in terms of scoping:

loadData <- reactive({
                if(length(input$loc)){
                        if(length(input$loc)>=1 & input$cond=="Location"){
                                for(i in 1:length(input$loc)) if(!exists(input$loc[i], envir=.GlobalEnv)) load(paste("data/",input$loc[i],".RData",sep=""), envir=.GlobalEnv)
                        } else {
                                if(!exists(input$loc[1], envir=.GlobalEnv)) load(paste("data/",input$loc[1],".RData",sep=""), envir=.GlobalEnv)
                        }
                }
        })
        
        checkData <- reactive({
                loadData()
                if(length(input$loc)){
                        exist <- c()
                        if(length(input$loc)>=1 & input$cond=="Location"){
                                for(i in 1:length(input$loc)) exist <- c(exist, exists(input$loc[i], envir=.GlobalEnv))
                        } else {
                                exist <- exists(input$loc[1], envir=.GlobalEnv)
                        }
                        return(all(exist))
                } else return(FALSE)
        })
        
        dat <- reactive({
                if(checkData()){
                        if(length(input$loc)>=1 & input$cond=="Location"){
                                dat <- c()
                                for(i in 1:length(input$loc)) dat <- rbind(dat,get(input$loc[i], envir=.GlobalEnv))
                        } else {
                                dat <- get(input$loc[1], envir=.GlobalEnv)
                        }
                } else dat <- NULL
                dat
        })

Related to the problem or not, in hindsight my choice to do this scoping for helping speed things up by allowing datasets loaded by one user to be already available to a subsequent, concurrent user, is probably are marginal benefit and I could remove it. But when I have seen this inability to update before, nothing like this has been in an app.

Thanks,
Matt

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: not all apps updatable on Spark server
parts:
Hi Matt,

Without digging deep into your code, it seems that your tabPanelAbout is read once when R process starts, and not with each browser access. So if the R process has been running for a while, you wouldn't have seen the changes. The fact that you see different behavior from your other apps on spark could be due to a restart of the R process for those apps. This could happen if the R process has been idle for a while or for some reason crashed.

One way to force shiny server to re-read such data is to create a "restart.txt" file in your app directory:

- Go to your application directory on spark
- Create an empty file called "restart.txt"  (Run this command: touch restart.txt)
- Then access your application in browser. 

This should update the content of About panel.

If you still see inconsistent behavior let us know. But my strong suspicion is that the updated data you have seen were due to a restart of R process.

Fereshteh

parts:
Matt,

Yesterday when I saw your post I checked on spark and noticed that for your temp_wind_events there was a running R process of a few days old, and a few active connections to it. So the content for this app haven't been updated since a few days back. None of your other apps had active connection/process. So if you have had accessed them yesterday, a new process would have started, and hence updated content.

When I checked earlier today I saw that the old process for temp_wind_events had terminated; a new process had started today. I don't know what happened. Whether because there was no more active sessions for a period of time, or something else. But either way, that is why you are now seeing the updated content today.

As for the restart.txt file, only the timestamp of this file is important. So really no need to delete it after usage since it will be outdated until the next time you need to run "touch restart.txt".

Keep us posted with your suggestions or issues.

Thanks,
Fereshteh
